# Concepts

- [[wiki/concepts/agent-harness|Agent harness]] — The runtime layer that owns the LLM–tool loop, memory, permissions and orchestration — and the layer users now swap the way they once swapped editors.
- [[wiki/concepts/agent-memory|Agent memory]] — The types of memory an agent keeps — operational state, semantic knowledge, episodes and preferences — and the rules for what gets written back.
- [[wiki/concepts/agent-skills|Agent skills]] — Reusable procedural knowledge packaged as a folder with a SKILL.md file — a cross-agent convention that no protocol defines.
- [[wiki/concepts/agentic-coding-loop|Agentic coding loop]] — Edit, run, read, fix — and the tool-selection criterion that follows: can the agent restart the thing it just changed, and see the error where it works?
- [[wiki/concepts/agentic-search|Agentic search]] — Letting the model write the database query itself, with the ontology in its prompt and a guard-rail stack around it.
- [[wiki/concepts/append-only-log|Append-only log]] — Store every extraction as an immutable observation and derive the queryable graph from it — buying provenance, replay and reversibility at the cost of RAM and a materialization step.
- [[wiki/concepts/cli-tools|CLIs as agent connectivity]] — Command-line tools as the cheapest connectivity mechanism for a local, sandboxed agent — strong on discovery and training-data familiarity, weak on distribution.
- [[wiki/concepts/connectivity-stack|Connectivity stack]] — The claim that agent connectivity is a layered choice — skills, CLIs and MCP, each for the job it fits — rather than a single mechanism to standardize on.
- [[wiki/concepts/context-layer|Context layer]] — The memory, notes and preferences that make an agent *yours* — the layer worth owning, because models and harnesses beneath it are commodities.
- [[wiki/concepts/context-rot|Context rot]] — As a context window fills, the signal-to-noise ratio collapses and the model degrades — the problem every retrieval decision in this wiki is ultimately optimizing against.
- [[wiki/concepts/data-fragmentation|Data fragmentation]] — Your knowledge lives in email, notes, documents and messages, in different formats behind different APIs — and no single retrieval ever spans them.
- [[wiki/concepts/database-scaling|Database scaling]] — Replicas, shards and the fact that RAM — not disk, not data size — is what actually bounds a knowledge-graph memory layer.
- [[wiki/concepts/durable-execution|Durable execution]] — Retries, result caching, checkpoints, scheduling and observability — the layer that decides whether a multi-step agent pipeline survives contact with production.
- [[wiki/concepts/embeddings|Embeddings]] — Where vectors get computed, hosted and paid for — and the decisions around them: summary versus chunk, dev versus prod, one interface across both.
- [[wiki/concepts/entity-resolution|Entity resolution]] — Deciding that "Art", "Arthur" and "Arthur Iusztin" are one node — the step that determines whether a knowledge graph accumulates knowledge or duplicates.
- [[wiki/concepts/governance|Governance and distribution]] — The requirement to ship, monitor and control business logic centrally — the axis on which servers beat CLIs and skill files once there are real users.
- [[wiki/concepts/graph-communities|Graph communities]] — Clusters of densely connected nodes, summarized by an LLM and stored beside them — the layer that makes top-down, overview-shaped retrieval possible.
- [[wiki/concepts/graph-extraction|Graph extraction]] — Turning text into typed triples — structured (ontology-guided), semi-structured (metadata and lineage, no LLM) and unstructured (free-form, for discovery only).
- [[wiki/concepts/graph-visualization|Graph visualization]] — Rendering the memory so a human can see it — in a notebook, a browser, or increasingly inside the chat itself.
- [[wiki/concepts/graphrag-ingestion|GraphRAG ingestion pipeline]] — The write path from raw sources to queryable memory — collect, clean, chunk, extract, resolve, embed, store — and the three steps in it that cost real money.
- [[wiki/concepts/hybrid-search|Hybrid search]] — Vector search for meaning, text search for the exact word, fused by rank — the seed-finding step that every retrieval path in this wiki starts from.
- [[wiki/concepts/inference-economics|Inference economics]] — Per-token versus GPU-hour, serverless versus reserved, and the one question that decides between them — is a human waiting?
- [[wiki/concepts/infrastructure-over-frameworks|Infrastructure over frameworks]] — Infrastructure tools solve problems that are genuinely hard to build; AI frameworks abstract the parts that are easy — and then fight your data model.
- [[wiki/concepts/knowledge-freshness|Knowledge freshness]] — Keeping a memory correct as it grows — decay, wrong extractions, stale beliefs — and the housekeeping the immutable log makes possible.
- [[wiki/concepts/knowledge-graph|Knowledge graph]] — Typed entities and relationships extracted from documents so retrieval can follow connections instead of only matching text — the structural half of the memory layer.
- [[wiki/concepts/materialized-view|Materialized view]] — The queryable graph rebuilt from the log by aggregation — where deduplication, property merging and embedding happen, and where the operational pain lives.
- [[wiki/concepts/mcp-apps|MCP Apps]] — Server-shipped user interfaces rendered by the client — an agent shipping its own UI, portable across every harness that speaks the protocol.
- [[wiki/concepts/mcp-primitives|MCP primitives]] — The small fixed set the protocol defines — tools, resources, prompts, sampling, elicitation, tasks — and the invocation semantics that follow from it.
- [[wiki/concepts/mcp-server-design|MCP server design]] — Designing a server for an agent to use rather than mirroring a REST API — few well-shaped tools, composition with existing servers, procedures as prompts.
- [[wiki/concepts/observability|Observability]] — Recording every model and tool call so a regression is a failing score rather than a user complaint — and so a bad answer can be traced to the call that produced it.
- [[wiki/concepts/pipeline-parallelism|Pipeline parallelism]] — Two independent axes — many runs across machines, many tasks inside a run — plus the rule that each stage's bottleneck must scale on its own.
- [[wiki/concepts/programmatic-tool-calling|Programmatic tool calling]] — Let the model write a script that composes tool calls in a sandbox instead of orchestrating them one inference step at a time.
- [[wiki/concepts/progressive-disclosure|Progressive disclosure]] — Give the model an index first and the detail only on request — the pattern that keeps tool schemas and retrieval results out of the context window until they are needed.
- [[wiki/concepts/provider-abstraction|Provider abstraction]] — One interface per model role, concrete implementations per environment — so tests, dev and production differ by config rather than by code.
- [[wiki/concepts/read-write-separation|Orchestrate the writes, never the reads]] — Ingestion is slow, expensive and failure-prone, so it belongs in a durable workflow; queries are cheap and idempotent, so orchestrating them only adds latency.
- [[wiki/concepts/server-side-orchestration|Server-side orchestration]] — Putting multi-step workflow logic inside the server as a composite tool, so it runs in one round-trip with a guaranteed order the model cannot alter.
- [[wiki/concepts/skills-over-mcp|Skills over MCP]] — Shipping skill files from an MCP server so procedural knowledge can be updated centrally — promising in the roadmap, inert in today's clients.
- [[wiki/concepts/unified-memory|Unified memory]] — One store holding documents, vectors, graph and history — so the agent has a single place to search and write, and no synchronization tax to pay.
